name: Ramp
text: Add a single high-contrast skip link at the top of every page. It’s the fastest way to help keyboard users bypass repetitive navigation blocks without cluttering the interface. The trade-off is one extra pixel of vertical space, but the benefit for users who rely on keyboard navigation outweighs any visual impact.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is sighted keyboard users missing the skip link entirely if it’s hidden until focus—it defeats the purpose of bypassing navigation. A better alternative is a skip link that’s always visible but visually subtle, like a small high-contrast icon in the top-left corner. Settle it by testing with both screen-reader and keyboard-only users to measure skip-link usage and frustration levels.

name: Ramp

Add a small, high-contrast skip icon always visible in the top-left corner of every page. It stays visible without distracting, so sighted keyboard users see it immediately while screen-reader users can still bypass navigation with one click. The trade-off is a tiny bit of screen real estate, but it solves the real problem: skip links that vanish until focus. Test it—users will reach content faster without clutter.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is sighted keyboard users treating the always-visible skip icon as decorative—ignoring it entirely because it doesn’t look clickable. A better alternative is a skip link that’s both visible *and* styled like a button, so sighted users recognize it as interactive. Settle it by testing with both keyboard-only and screen-reader users to confirm it’s noticed and used.
